name: Alghero-Fertilia Airport
before:
One of Sardinia's three main airports, 8 km north north west of Alghero, with Olbia serving the north east and Cagliari the south. It is also known as Alghero-Fertilia, after the village next door, and as Riviera del Corallo.

The runway is 3,000 metres, one of the longest in Italy and a good deal more than the traffic needs. It got that way in the mid 1970s, having started in 1938 as a military field with just 700 metres of runway during the war.

Getting around the island is straightforward from here. ARST, the Sardinian transport operator, runs buses into Alghero and also to Sassari, Olbia and Cagliari, with seasonal private services from Cagliari and Santa Teresa Gallura. By road the SS 42 runs into town and the SS 131 Carlo Felice and SS 291 reach the rest of the island.

Alitalia ran a flight school here from 1980, training up to a hundred pilots a year, until it closed in March 2003.
